page: UpCloud PREMIUM-4xCPU-16GB is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor, running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled with a 150 GB SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU architecture is x86_64 and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier single-core performance, with the stress-ng single-core test and Geekbench single-core score of 2557.0 both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also demonstrate top-tier execution speeds. Conversely, multi-core performance metrics, such as the Geekbench multi-core score of 7841.0 and the stress-ng multi-core CPU test, fall within the average range. Memory performance presents a notable tradeoff; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 798.33 GB/sec, the overall PassMark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25%.

This hardware profile is well-suited for workloads that benefit from strong single-threaded performance but do not require sustained, high-bandwidth memory access. Suitable applications include static web serving, software compilation, text processing, and moderate database operations, as evidenced by the average Redis SET throughput of 8.73 million operations per second. The shared CPU allocation model offers a cost-effective entry point for general-purpose computing, balancing multi-core capacity and local SSD storage without the premium cost of dedicated, high-density memory configurations.
